phases.name: Base
phases.description: Build aerobic foundation and establish training routine
phases.focus: Consistent mileage and long run progression
phases.coachNote: No speed work yet. Focus on building the habit of 4 runs per week. Long runs at easy conversational pace.

phases.name: Build
phases.description: Introduce intervals, extend tempo runs, and add marathon pace segments to long runs
phases.focus: Speed endurance, threshold development, and race pace familiarization
phases.coachNote: This is the hardest phase. Prioritize sleep and nutrition. Marathon pace blocks in long runs are the most important sessions.

phases.name: Peak
phases.description: Longest runs with extended marathon pace blocks at peak volume
phases.coachNote: Longest runs of the plan. MP blocks simulate late-race fatigue. Practice race-day routine: gear, breakfast, hydration.

phases.name: Taper
phases.description: Reduce volume while preserving intensity for race-day freshness
phases.focus: Recovery, glycogen replenishment, and mental preparation
phases.coachNote: Volume drops ~60% by race week. Stay off your feet, hydrate well, carb-load 2-3 days before the race.

Tue.name: Easy Run
Tue.coachNote: Keep HR in zone2. If you feel good, don't speed up — save it for Thursday.

Thu.name: Easy Run + Strides
Thu.description: Steady easy run finishing with 5 gentle strides
Thu.coachNote: Strides = 20-30sec smooth accelerations with full recovery between each.

Sat.name: Long Run LSD
Sat.description: Long slow distance at easy pace
Sat.coachNote: Start slower than you think you need to. Bring water for runs over 60 minutes.

Tue.name: 800m Intervals
Tue.description: Warmup 2km easy + 6×800m @5:00/km (400m jog recovery) + Cooldown 2km easy
Tue.coachNote: Early build: 5×800m. Late build: 7×800m. Jog the recoveries — keep moving.

Wed.name: Easy Recovery Run
Wed.coachNote: Shakeout run. If you're tired, walking part of it is fine.

Thu.name: Tempo Run
Thu.coachNote: Tempo pace = threshold. Breathing is deep and controlled. Extend to 30min in weeks 8-10.

Sat.name: Long Run + MP
Sat.description: Long run with 8km at marathon pace (5:41/km) in the middle
Sat.coachNote: First half easy, MP block in the middle, finish easy. Practice taking gels every 40-45min.

Tue.name: 1600m Intervals
Tue.description: Warmup 2km easy + 4×1600m @5:10/km (600m jog recovery) + Cooldown 2km easy
Tue.coachNote: Long intervals at threshold pace. Hold consistent splits — no fading on the last rep.

Wed.name: Easy Recovery Run
Wed.coachNote: Active recovery. Keep it truly easy.

Thu.name: Marathon Pace Run
Thu.coachNote: Lock into MP. Make it feel effortless — this is your race rhythm.

Sat.name: Long Run + Extended MP
Sat.description: Long run with 14km at marathon pace in the second half
Sat.coachNote: Dress rehearsal. Practice everything: pre-run meal, gels every 40min, hydration. MP blocks in the second half simulate late-race conditions.

Tue.name: Easy Run + Strides
Tue.description: Easy run with 5×20sec strides at race pace
Tue.coachNote: Strides maintain neuromuscular sharpness without fatigue. Week 16: skip strides, just easy 30min.

Thu.name: Short Tempo
Thu.coachNote: Short tempo to keep the engine primed. Week 16: replace with 30min easy run.

Sat.name: Long Run (Taper)
Sat.description: Week 14: 20km easy. Week 15: 14km easy. Week 16: RACE DAY — 42.2km. Sub 4:00!
Sat.coachNote: Week 14: last moderate long run. Week 15: light, stay off feet. Race week: carb-load, hydrate. Start conservatively (5:50/km), settle into 5:41/km. Negative split if you can.

trainingPlan.name: 16-Week Marathon Sub 4:00
trainingPlan.description: A 16-week plan for runners who have completed a half marathon and want to run a sub-4:00 marathon (target pace 5:41/km). Builds from 14km to 32km long runs with progressive marathon-pace blocks.
trainingPlan.goal: Complete a marathon in under 4 hours (sub 4:00)
